newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--French voters gave the European Union a message for a more social union over the weekend with the Left's victory. Prime Minister Costas Simitis has invited French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin to visit Athens later this month with other European leftists to discuss common goals and strategies.
--Coalition of the Left and Progress leader Nikos Constantopoulos responds to overtures from ruling party PASOK for a centre-Left dialogue.
--One of the ten wealthiest men in the world, shipowner George Livanos died yesterday at the age of 70.
--Yesterday's election win in France by the Left was a personal defeat for Jacques Chirac - the result now means that only two of the EU's 15 countries are governed by the Right.
--The real estate market has seen a rise in prices of up to 10 percent.

--The government is promoting part-time positions in the public sector to get around the problem of permanent tenure. Also on the negotiating table with unions and employers is incomes policy for the next few years and overtime policies.

--Former public order minister Stelios Papathemelis says his ministry knew the names of people associated with the November 17 terrorist group but failed to act. November 17 last week killed Greek shipowner Costas Peratikos in the streets of Piraeus.
